reasons: The settings are plain and typical.

terms.meaning: Descriptions of what a piece of code is and what it can do, used by the compiler to catch mistakes.
A shared settings file that this file builds on.

used_by: The root typecheck command, which runs the check for this folder.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Compiler settings for scripts
sections.what: Sets the source and output folders and limits the available types to Node.js.
sections.why: Matches the scripts' runtime, which is Node.js.
sections.watch_out: Adding browser types here is only needed for browser code, so keep the list to Node.js unless that changes.

summary: Compiler settings for the scripts folder. It reads from src, writes to dist, and limits type help to Node.js.
purpose: Lets the typecheck command check the scripts code.
why: Likely reason: the scripts run on Node.js, so only Node.js types are needed. The code does not state this.
how: Inherits the shared base settings, sets dist as the output folder and src as the source folder, and restricts the available types to node.
inputs: The src folder and the base config at tsconfig.base.json.
outputs: Type-check results, and output files in dist if any are written.
risks: Browser-only code placed here will fail the check because only Node.js types are allowed.
debug: If the check reports missing names, look at the types list and the base config.
